bug_semantics: When the opt-in Management API is enabled with its token left empty, its authentication middleware treats the empty secret as successful authentication. The server listens on all interfaces at port 9820, and an unauthenticated remote POST to /api/v1/cron can copy attacker-controlled JSON exec text into a persisted CronJob. The cron scheduler identifies a nonempty Exec as a shell job and ultimately runs that text through the configured shell, so the attacker obtains command execution when the job fires; later code also added an immediate /api/v1/cron/{id}/exec trigger, but that was not necessary for the original scheduled-execution path.
flaw_origin: The vulnerable trust-boundary crossing was created in one change: c2681402a7686294174a263e31245a52d4fea380 added the network-facing Management API, deliberately made authenticate return true for an empty token, registered the cron endpoints behind that fail-open middleware, and assigned untrusted req.Exec directly to CronJob.Exec. The shell-capable CronJob and its sh -c execution sink already existed in the parent; c2681402 is the smallest commit that made that sink reachable from an unauthenticated remote management request.
ai_marker: BIC commit object c2681402a7686294174a263e31245a52d4fea380 has author and committer chenhg5 <chenhonggui@wps.cn> and contains the exact message markers 'generated by llmgit' and 'Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>'.
evidence: Advisory GHSA-v2jj-5g64-rxp4 / CVE-2026-76761 names core/engine.go shellExecCommand and Management API command injection through exec; first-party report https://github.com/chenhg5/cc-connect/issues/1489 documents the complete POST /api/v1/cron -> CronJob.Exec -> scheduler -> shellExecCommand chain and maintainer confirmation. At BIC c2681402a7686294174a263e31245a52d4fea380, core/management.go:55-85 starts an HTTP server on :<port>, lines 69-71 register /api/v1/cron, lines 96-124 wrap requests but return true when m.token is empty, and lines 922-973 decode CronAddRequest and assign Exec: req.Exec before AddJob. The same commit adds cmd/cc-connect/main.go startup wiring and config/config.go ManagementConfig; enabled is opt-in/default false, but token is an unchecked string and the example calls it required without enforcing that requirement. In immediate parent 968cd9142dd7a9f7f1ea09a45cb7329761c44abb, git grep shows core/cron.go already defines CronJob.Exec and core/engine.go:613 runs job.Exec with exec.CommandContext(ctx, 'sh', '-c', job.Exec), but git ls-tree for core/management.go is empty. Direct tree comparison reports 'A core/management.go', proving the remote fail-open path and req.Exec assignment are absent from the immediate parent. git log -L 325,327:core/management.go HEAD attributes the empty-token true return only to c2681402; git log -L 1572,1575 attributes Exec: req.Exec only to c2681402; git log -S 'if m.token == ""' --all likewise returns only c2681402. The BIC is a one-parent public commit, not a merge; no smaller public member commit is present or referenced, so squash decomposition is not applicable. Version boundary: v1.2.2-beta.1 (ecea1ef36d86bb70dd633fb342f655d108ea52cb) predates the file, while the v1.2.2-beta.1..v1.2.2-beta.2 diff adds core/management.go and git tag --contains c2681402 starts at v1.2.2-beta.2; c2681402 is also contained in advisory-named v1.4.1. No fix was found: git grep at v1.4.1, v1.5.0, and audited HEAD 80713167d17b3f2a3906efc3b14b3acab39766e4 still finds both 'if m.token == ""' and 'Exec: req.Exec' in core/management.go. Thus the textual 'up to 1.4.1' boundary reflects the latest version considered by the advisory, not a patched 1.4.2 boundary; v1.5.0 and HEAD remain vulnerable. BIC-only AI evidence comes from git cat-file commit c2681402 and the public commit object at https://github.com/chenhg5/cc-connect/commit/c2681402a7686294174a263e31245a52d4fea380, which carry the llmgit and Claude co-author markers.
reasoning: The preexisting cron shell facility is not by itself the reported Management API vulnerability: before c2681402 there was no core/management.go and therefore no network management route accepting attacker-controlled cron JSON. Commit c2681402 completes the vulnerable lifecycle in the smallest recorded unit by exposing the API on all interfaces, authorizing every request whenever the configured token is empty, accepting exec, and storing it in the already shell-executable CronJob. Its direct parent lacks the entire file, while both origin-tracing methods identify c2681402 as the first writer of the decisive fail-open check and remote-to-shell assignment. The first vulnerable tagged boundary is v1.2.2-beta.2 and the mechanism persists through v1.4.1, v1.5.0, and the audited HEAD, so there is no fix SHA to record. AI attribution is closed from the BIC commit object alone: the same causal first-writer commit explicitly says it was generated by llmgit and co-authored by Claude. That satisfies AI_ROOT_CAUSE rather than AI_CODE_FLAWED because the AI-marked BIC itself created the flawed authentication and dataflow, not merely a later refactor or fix.
remaining_gap: Unpatched as of audited HEAD 80713167d17b3f2a3906efc3b14b3acab39766e4 (2026-08-28): no fix_sha or direct_fix_sha exists, and the advisory's 'up to 1.4.1' wording does not identify a patched release even though v1.5.0 and HEAD retain the vulnerable lines.
